failures.name: TestHoughLines_Calc
failures.reason: Op is functionally correct on CoreX (proven by TestCorexHoughLinesFunctional). Only the hard-coded NVIDIA column count (1588 vs ~1598) fails.

failures.name: TestHoughLines_CalcWithStream
failures.reason: Same as TestHoughLines_Calc (count-only divergence; functionally correct).

failures.name: TestSparsePyrLKOpticalFlow_Calc
failures.reason: SparsePyrLKOpticalFlow::create symbol exists but .calc throws throw_no_cuda ('The library is compiled without CUDA support', core/private.cuda.hpp:110). The sparse-LK calc kernel is not built with CUDA in this libopencv_cudaoptflow.so — no GPU sparse-LK path to call. Unfixable at repo layer without rebuilding CoreX OpenCV.

failures.name: TestHoughSegment_Calc
failures.reason: SIGILL (illegal instruction) inside CoreX cudaimgproc HoughSegmentDetector detect kernel. createHoughSegmentDetector symbol present; the compiled device kernel emits an illegal instruction on ivcore11. Unfixable at repo layer.

failures.name: TestHoughSegment_CalcWithStream
failures.reason: Same as TestHoughSegment_Calc (SIGILL in CoreX HoughSegment kernel).

notes:
After two repo-local workarounds (GPU flip via remap; tolerance-based HoughLines verification), 40/45 upstream CUDA binding tests pass on real Iluvatar BI-V150 GPUs, plus the added functional test. Remaining 3 hard failures are defects inside the pre-installed CoreX OpenCV 4.6.0 libraries (sparse-LK not built with CUDA; HoughSegment kernel SIGILL) and cannot be fixed without touching /usr/local/corex. The 2 HoughLines 'failures' are functionally correct and differ only in an exact golden count.
